title: Inverse Scaling: When Bigger Isn’t Better

bias_targets.target: Social bias (Gender, Religion, Race, Ethnicity, Nationality)
bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing model responses in ambiguous versus unambiguous contexts (e.g., reviewing the BBQ dataset) to evaluate whether language models rely on stereotypical associations and skewed historical distributions learned during pretraining.

Evaluating models using the 'Repetitive Algebra' task, which provides a sequence of few-shot examples, to test whether the model simply copies the most recently seen answer in the prompt rather than genuinely performing the required computation.

Testing models on 'Distractor Tasks' (such as the 'Sig Figs' or 'Into the Unknown' tasks) to observe if they unintentionally substitute the difficult, instructed task with a superficially similar but easier subtask they already know how to perform.

Reviewing prior literature to highlight how alternative training objectives (like Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback) can introduce partisan biases, such as favoring liberal answers to political questions, which grow worse with model scale.
